rationale: There is strong qualitative support across multiple cohorts that corpus callosum hypoplasia and cerebellar or cerebral atrophy represent hallmark neuroimaging features of MAPK8IP3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Platzer et al., 2019; Iwasawa et al., 2019). However, the claim that structural neuroimaging abnormalities occur in >85% of all cases is conflicted: the formal disease entity is designated 'Neurodevelopmental disorder with or without variable brain abnormalities' (OMIM #618443), and Platzer et al. note that consistent brain anomalies were specifically prominent among individuals harboring recurrent missense variants rather than truncating variants, indicating genotype-dependent penetrance rather than a uniform >85% rate across all affected individuals.

evidence.text: Platzer et al. identified 13 unrelated individuals with de novo variants in MAPK8IP3 and observed that brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants within the cohort.

source.title: De novo variants in MAPK8IP3 cause intellectual disability with variable brain anomalies
source.quote: Brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants.

evidence.text: Iwasawa et al. reported five individuals from four families with recurrent de novo MAPK8IP3 variants whose core phenotype specifically included cerebral atrophy and corpus callosum hypoplasia along with spastic diplegia and intellectual disability.

source.title: Recurrent de novo MAPK8IP3 variants cause neurological phenotypes
source.quote: The core phenotype includes spastic diplegia, intellectual disability, cerebral atrophy, and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

evidence.text: The official OMIM clinical synopsis and title define OMIM #618443 as 'Neurodevelopmental disorder with or without variable brain abnormalities', indicating that structural neuroimaging anomalies are not obligate and can be absent in a subset of confirmed cases.

source.title: Entry - #618443 - NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER ...
source.quote: cerebellar atrophy, loss of white matter volume, thin corpus callosum, and perisylvian polymicrogyria.

conflicts: While corpus callosum hypoplasia and cerebellar/cerebral atrophy are primary hallmark imaging features, the >85% penetrance threshold across all variant types is contradicted by the disorder's formal classification as 'with or without variable brain abnormalities' and Platzer et al.'s finding that brain anomalies were predominantly consistent in recurrent missense variants rather than all 13 individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of structural brain malformations stratified by variant type (missense vs. loss-of-function/truncating) across all reported MAPK8IP3 cases?
new_directions.rationale: Platzer et al. noted that brain anomalies were consistent primarily in recurrent missense variants, suggesting loss-of-function variants may present without overt structural brain abnormalities.
